endorsements.quote: Before implementing a model in a specific location, it is recommended to conduct a local validation study.
Consider to monitor performance over time and to (dynamically) update the model, in particular when calibration is problematic [ 31 , 32 , 53 ].
When validating a prediction model, inclusion of multiple settings or locations allows to study performance heterogeneity across settings [ 10 , 39 , 43 , 44 ].

Follow the TRIPOD reporting guideline (Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis), including the newly available TRIPOD-Cluster extension where appropriate [ 49 – 52 ].
We stress that calibration assessment in the external validation sample is at least as important as discrimination [ 9 ].
Consider to monitor performance over time and to (dynamically) update the model, in particular when calibration is problematic [ 31 , 32 , 53 ].

unlisted_practices: Developers should include multiple settings or locations when developing a prediction model, such as through multicenter or individual participant data studies.
Developers should quantify performance heterogeneity using internal-external cross-validation.
Developers should standardize predictor variable definitions and measurement protocols to reduce measurement heterogeneity.
Developers should investigate operator-induced measurement variability.
Developers should consider including operational or population-level characteristics, such as type of center, as predictors.
Evaluation teams should use adequate sample size for validation studies, with at least 100 to 200 cases in the smallest outcome category.
Developers should make the prediction model and predictor definitions available to allow independent external validation.
Researchers should avoid claiming a prediction model is 'externally valid' or 'validated' based on a single external validation or simplistic c-statistic thresholds.
Researchers should shift focus from developing new prediction models to conducting more extensive, well-conducted, well-reported validation studies of promising models.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective article arguing that clinical prediction models require ongoing validation, monitoring, and updating rather than assuming a single validation proves they are universally valid.
